TEST FILE ONLY. This is made-up text to test the code. It is not medical advice and not a real source.

Diarrhoea at home. A child with loose motions loses a lot of water. Give oral rehydration solution, called ORS, after every loose motion. Mix the ORS packet with clean boiled water. Keep feeding the child and continue breastfeeding. Give zinc for 14 days to help the child recover. Take the child to a health centre if the child cannot drink, has blood in the stool, or becomes very sleepy.

Zinc for children. Zinc helps the gut heal after diarrhoea and lowers the chance of another episode. Give zinc every day for the full 14 days, even if the loose motions stop earlier. Zinc 20 mg is given once a day for children above six months.

Newborn cord care. Keep the umbilical cord clean and dry. Do not apply anything on the cord. Fold the nappy below the cord. Wash your hands with soap before touching the baby. Take the baby to the health centre if the cord becomes red, swollen or smells bad.

Exclusive breastfeeding. Give only breast milk for the first six months. Breastfeeding protects the newborn from infections. Start breastfeeding within one hour of birth. Do not give water, honey or other foods in the first six months.

Fever at home. Keep the person lightly dressed and give plenty of fluids. Tepid sponging with a wet cloth can help bring down the temperature. Paracetamol 500 mg tablets may be used by adults as the doctor advises. You have a viral fever if the joints are paining. Go to the health centre if the fever lasts more than three days.

Blood pressure care. Eating less salt helps control blood pressure. Walk every day and avoid tobacco. Check blood pressure regularly at the health centre. Go to the hospital at once if there is a very bad headache with chest pain.

Hand washing. Wash your hands with soap and clean water before eating and after using the toilet. Hand washing prevents diarrhoea and other infections.
